newsitem.title: USA: Several factors keeping US inflation low--Phillips.
newsitem.headline: Several factors keeping US inflation low--Phillips.

text.p: Federal Reserve Governor Susan Phillips said on Wednesday that a confluence of factors had combined to create a benign U.S. inflation environment.
These included slow growth abroad, low costs and high productivity of U.S. firms, and improvements in the measurements of the Consumer Price Index.
She said that there had been some buildup in wage pressure but this had not immediately translated into higher prices.
"The fact that some of the other economies have been somewhat slower recently has provided some relief to us on the inflation front," Phillips said at a business group luncheon here.
She also said that U.S. industry had played a part in cutting inflation.
"The enormous impetus by U.S. industry to control costs, to improve productivity, are helping to control inflation," she said.
"We have to recognize that we've seen some buildup in wage pressures. I think that that doesn't necessarily translate immediately into price increases," Phillips said.
Phillips also said that recent improvements of the CPI had made that figure lower than it would otherwise have been.
